title: Twofold coverings of the Hamming cube: a Lean-verified K(8,1,2) >= 61, and an even-n theorem improving five published bounds
description:

The five published entries this improves

The ratio to the old bound tends to 1, but the additive gap grows like (2/3)*2^n/n^2 and is unbounded, so the improvement does not run out.

K(n,R,mu) is the minimum size of a binary code in F_2^n such that every word has at least mu codewords within Hamming distance R. K(8,1,2) is the first unknown term of OEIS A004045; the published record was 59 <= K(8,1,2) <= 64. This package establishes 61 <= K(8,1,2) <= 64.

1. A lower bound for all even n. An elementary parity/excess argument gives |C| >= ceil(3 * 2^(n+1) / (3n+2)) for even n. This strictly improves the best published lower bound at five table positions (n = 8, 10, 12, 14, 16) and reproves the exact value K(6,1,2) = 20 with no computer search. In particular K(8,1,2) >= 60, established by three independent routes: the theorem; an exact-rational SCIP-to-VIPR certificate refuting |C| = 59, accepted by viprchk (included, 3.6 GB); and agreement of two independent floating-point solvers (evidence, not a certificate).

2. K(8,1,2) >= 61, formalised. A refutation of |C| = 60 via Delsarte nonnegativity in sum-of-squares form, an antipode row, and a layer Farkas certificate. It is formalised in Lean 4 / mathlib with zero sorrys:

le_card_of_isDoubleCover : forall (C : Finset V), IsDoubleCover C -> 61 <= C.card
  depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]

No sorryAx and no native_decide. The trusted base is Lean's kernel plus twelve short definitions that a reader can check by eye; non-vacuity is verified separately (the space has 256 words, and IsDoubleCover is proved both satisfiable and non-trivial), and every declaration's axiom trace is printed by lake build Mcov.Audit.

3. Where a better code cannot live. Any non-identity automorphism has a power of prime order, so it suffices to rule out prime-order ones; all 28 prime-order classes of Aut(Q_8) = F_2^8 : S_8 are infeasible at <= 63, so every <= 63 double covering is asymmetric (on a weaker footing than the other results). An independent 746-class cyclic sweep agrees on every verdict. Caveat: only 4 of the 28 are machine-certified; the other 24, all of order 2, are floating-point solver verdicts, and the package says so. A parity argument narrows 20 of those 24 to a single equality instance.

Reproduction. ./reproduce.sh runs 12 self-asserting checks in about a minute, using the Python standard library apart from one step that needs scipy for small LP control cases, and exits non-zero if any fails. The Lean development is a separate ~4-minute build.

What this does not settle. The upper bound remains 64 and is untouched by this work. That bound is older than it is usually credited: it is already in the 1993 table of Haemaelaeinen, Honkala, Kaikkonen and Litsyn as the doubling K(8,1,2) <= 2*K(7,1,2) = 64, and Oestergaard's 1995 tabu-search paper, which improves 27 upper bounds in that table, does not improve this one. No human has reviewed the proof or the Lean definitions. Novelty is not claimed: Krotov and Potapov already apply Delsarte nonnegativity to a covering code's own distance distribution, and a Chen-Li preprint cited in the literature could not be located. What is claimed is correctness, and for K >= 61 that rests on Lean's kernel rather than on judgement.
